analysis.title: The Weekly Brief (Market Insights, 26 October 2026)
key_insights: US consumer spending has stayed robust this year, which partly explains the resilience of US economic growth.
Buoyant equity markets have supported spending through a wealth effect. US households invest a relatively high share of savings in equities, so stock gains can raise willingness to spend.
Household net worth relative to disposable income has risen. Most of the increase over the past year came from gains in financial assets, per the latest data.
Spending has been supported even though some measures of inflation-adjusted wage growth have turned negative amid higher energy prices.
Headwinds remain, including elevated interest rates, but spending is likely to stay supportive for growth, particularly as the household savings rate has further room to fall.

Week ahead: Fed rate decision Wednesday (prior 4.00%), ECB rate decision Thursday (prior 2.50%), US Sep core and headline PCE and Q3 GDP Thursday, Bank of Japan decision Friday (prior 1.25%), UK Autumn Budget Wednesday.
Week to 23 October: MSCI Europe -1.5%, S&P 500 -0.5%, MSCI EM -2.5%, MSCI China -4.6%, TOPIX -2.5%. Communication services fell 5.4% and materials 3.9%, while healthcare rose 2.0% and energy 1.2%.
Brent is at $113/bbl, up 3.0% on the week and 86.1% year to date. Gold is at $3,996/oz, down 4.4% on the week and 7.6% year to date.
The US 10-year yield is 5.00%, down 8bps on the week and up 84bps year to date. UK 10-year is 5.36%, Germany 3.34%, Japan 2.80%.
Global high yield spreads widened 15bps on the week to 363bps. Global IG spreads widened 7bps to 96bps. VIX is 19 versus 20 a week earlier and 15 at the start of the year.
